question: Within the F1 2.1.0 cohort (identical to 2.0.0), (a) does a per-segment model choice made on validation origins beat the single validation champion, and (b) do interval scale factors fitted on validation origins bring 80% coverage nearer 80% without losing pinball? Also: where do the models fail (demand segments, bias, calibration)?
reuse: F1 2.1.0 (weekday-corrected TCN) cohort, panel, selected configurations and its test-origin artifacts; no new hyper-parameter search

segmentation.method: Syntetos-Boylan on the 365 days up to (and including) each origin; only information available at the origin

rules_frozen_on_validation.segment_choice: for each segment, the family with the lowest mean pinball over the validation origins (series assigned to segments at each origin); a segment with fewer than 10 validation series falls back to the overall validation champion (tcn)
rules_frozen_on_validation.interval_scaling: per family, one scale s on the grid 0.30..3.00 step 0.01 applied as [q50 - s(q50-q10), q50 + s(q90-q50)], chosen so validation 80% coverage is closest to 0.80 (ties: smaller s); q50 unchanged

test_use: test origins are scored once with the frozen rules; they were already seen by F1 1.0.0 and 2.0.0, so every test result here is exploratory, not confirmatory (D-042)
comparisons: segment composite vs tcn (per-product MAE and pinball, averaged over test origins, product-level paired bootstrap 2,000 resamples)
